title: Public-facing web application
description: A marketing website with a customer portal login, several public-facing forms, and a content-management backend used by editorial staff. Reachable from the open internet with no network-level access restriction. Use this template as a starting point for any small-to-medium site that combines public content, a customer login, and a staff-facing CMS.

risks.title: Customer account takeover
risks.description: An attacker gains control of a customer's portal account, exposing their stored profile data and letting the attacker act as that customer within the portal.

risks.title: Public site defacement or malicious content injection
risks.description: An attacker modifies public-facing pages through the CMS backend, replacing legitimate content with defacement, malware links, or fraudulent material shown to every visitor.

risks.title: Exposure of personal data submitted through public forms
risks.description: Data submitted through the contact, quote-request, or newsletter-signup forms is read, exfiltrated, or dumped in bulk from the underlying store, exposing names, emails, and free-text submissions.

risks.title: Public site unavailability
risks.description: The public site or customer portal becomes unreachable or unusably slow, turning away visitors and blocking customers from logging in for the duration of the incident.

attacks.title: Credential stuffing against the customer portal login
attacks.description: Automated login attempts using username/password pairs leaked from unrelated breaches, run against the portal's public login form until a reused credential succeeds.

attacks.title: Stored cross-site scripting through a public comment or review field
attacks.description: An attacker submits a crafted script through a public-facing text field that is rendered unescaped to later visitors or to staff reviewing submissions in the CMS, executing in their browser session.

attacks.title: Cross-site request forgery against the CMS admin panel
attacks.description: A logged-in editor is lured to a malicious page that silently submits a forged request to the CMS admin panel, performing a content or settings change the editor never intended.

attacks.title: Remote code execution through an outdated CMS plugin
attacks.description: A known, publicly disclosed vulnerability in an installed CMS plugin or theme is exploited to run arbitrary code on the server hosting the CMS backend.

references.title: Improper Control of Generation of Code

attacks.title: SQL injection through the contact or quote-request form
attacks.description: Unsanitised input on a public lead-generation form allows an attacker to manipulate the backing query and read or export rows from the submissions table, including other visitors' data.

attacks.title: Volumetric DDoS against the public site
attacks.description: A traffic flood aimed at the site's public origin, saturating bandwidth or connection capacity and pushing legitimate visitors out.

defences.title: Multi-factor authentication for the customer portal
defences.description: An optional TOTP-based second factor customers can enable on their portal account, enforced automatically after a suspicious-login flag.

attack-credential-stuffing-portal.rationale: Blocks a stuffed credential from completing login on the subset of accounts that have enrolled; adoption is currently well under half of the customer base.

defences.title: Cyber insurance policy
defences.description: Annual policy covering breach-response, notification, and a portion of regulatory-fine costs following a confirmed data-exposure incident.

attack-credential-stuffing-portal.rationale: Policy deductible and sub-limit mean roughly a third of the loss on an incident reached through this path is reimbursed on average.

attack-sqli-contact-form.rationale: Slightly lower coverage than the login path, since a known-vulnerability finding of this kind is more likely to fall under the policy's negligence exclusion.

defences.title: Web application firewall in front of the public site
defences.description: Managed WAF filtering known injection and script-injection patterns and absorbing a portion of flood traffic before it reaches the origin.

attack-xss-comment-form.rationale: Catches common script-injection payload shapes but an encoded or fragmented payload aimed at this specific field can still pass through.

attack-sqli-contact-form.rationale: Blocks most known SQL-injection payload signatures at the edge, before they reach the form handler.

attack-ddos-volumetric.rationale: Absorbs moderate floods but has no dedicated scrubbing capacity behind it, so a large volumetric attack still degrades service.

defences.title: Server-side input validation and output encoding on public forms
defences.description: Strict server-side validation of submitted field types plus context-aware output encoding wherever user-submitted text is later rendered.

attack-xss-comment-form.rationale: Output encoding neutralises the large majority of script-injection attempts regardless of how they are obfuscated, independent of the WAF's signature matching.

attack-sqli-contact-form.rationale: Parameterised queries and type validation on the form handler remove the injection point directly rather than filtering for known payload shapes.

defences.title: CSRF tokens on the CMS admin panel
defences.description: Per-session anti-CSRF tokens required on every state-changing request submitted through the CMS admin panel.

attack-csrf-admin-panel.rationale: A correctly implemented per-session token makes a forged cross-site request unable to complete, since the attacker's page cannot read or supply a valid token.

defences.title: Scheduled CMS plugin and theme patch management
defences.description: A recurring process to inventory installed CMS plugins and themes against a public vulnerability feed and apply security updates on a fixed schedule.

attack-cms-plugin-rce.rationale: Closes the window between public disclosure of a plugin vulnerability and a fix being applied, which is when most opportunistic exploitation happens.

defences.title: Legacy on-premises intrusion-prevention appliance (decommission planned)
defences.description: An older rule-based network appliance that predates the managed WAF, previously relied on for basic flood mitigation. Left in place during the transition but no longer actively tuned.

attack-ddos-volumetric.rationale: Only ever mitigated small-scale floods and offered negligible protection against the volumes seen from modern botnets.
